thread:
Alex: Taking the evening rotation (18:00-02:00). Quick rundown of what changed since yesterday — keeping this short.
Maria: Thanks — passing notes to you. Two config deploys landed at 15:20 and 16:10, both kube-rollouts. No errors in the deploy logs but saw a small blip in prometheus latency around 15:30.
Devon: That blip was the autoscaler bouncing during a noisy batch job from customer X. We throttled them at 15:40, and autoscale smoothed out.
Alex: Good to know. Watch for CPU spikes on inference-prod-2 and any throttled pods. If you see >70% sustained for 2m, escalate to Samir.
oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled canary for model-migrate-v2 at 23:00 UTC — 5% traffic for 30m, automatic rollback on error.
Maria: Canary details: route via region-us-west, fallback policy set to redwood-embed-small. Healthcheck endpoint /health returns 200 for canary.
Joanne: Heads up — eval-run-402 is finishing tonight (expected 21:30). If it reports quality regressions, we'll pause canary.
Alex: Action items for me tonight: 1) Monitor canary at 23:00; 2) Keep an eye on latency SLOs for chat-gateway; 3) Merge Samir's quickfix PR if green.
Samir: PR is #4128 — fixes a race in KV cache invalidation. CI is flaky on macos runner but linux tests passed. If you merge, please re-run the e2e.
Devon: Quick commands I used earlier:
```
# check rollout
kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/model-migrate --watch
# tail canary logs
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=model-migrate -c runtime --tail=200
```
Alex: Oncall notes: current pager load 0, no active incidents. Expected noisy windows: 22:30-00:00 (batch starts), and 23:00 canary. If latency spikes >200ms p99, toggle canary to 0% and ping infra.
Maria: Cover swap request — I need to step out 20:00-21:00. Devon can you cover that slot?
Devon: Yep I can take 20:00-21:00. I'll monitor chat-gateway and take over canary watch if Alex needs a break.
Alex: Thanks. If anyone needs the immediate rotation swap, DM me.
Joanne: FYI — there's a known flaky alert: redis-connection-drop on cache-prod occasionally during peak writes. We have a mitigation doc at https://wiki.redwood/ops/redis-mitigation — follow steps 2-4 if you see it.
Samir: If you hit redis alerts, also check our cached-prefix hit rate metric `cache.prefix_hit` — dropping hit rate often correlates before the drops.
Alex: Final: logging note — I turned on debug for model-migrate canary only. If logs get noisy, toggle back with `kubectl annotate` snippet in the runbook.
Maria: Thanks Alex — leaving a pinned checklist in the channel. :thumbsup:
Alex: Leaving now, Devon will be primary from 20:00-21:00, Samir on-call for escalations. Ping in thread for async handoff notes later.
